title: coloring-aware-lru-slab-warmup-and-spillback-smoother
author: Asha Mehta
release_notes: Introduces a coloring-aware LRU tier and spillback smoothing to reduce fragmentation and tail latency under mixed tenant workloads. Non-breaking; can be toggled via runtime flags.
description: Motivation: under mixed-tenant traffic we observed growing fragmentation and noisy eviction storms when large items were interleaved with many small ones. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) a lightweight 'coloring' layer that semantically buckets KV entries by allocation class and recent access pattern to bias evictions and prevent hot items from dragging cold slot fragmentation, and (2) a spillback smoothing controller that rate-limits paged spill operations using a token-bucket tied to the serving scheduler so that spill bursts don't interfere with latency-sensitive inference requests. Design highlights: coloring is implemented as a metadata byte per slab slot (packed into the slab header) and an epoched LRU per color; eviction picks candidates from the coldest color first but can steal across colors when under memory pressure. Warmup: when a slab is rehydrated after spill, the warmup walker replays a sampled recent-access index to avoid immediate eviction of freshly-resident hot items. Spillback smoothing: the controller tracks outstanding async spill tasks and the moving-average CPU/IO stall metric; it gates new spill submissions and signals the scheduler to prefer non-eviction work during high latency windows. Changeset: adds coloring metadata and epoched LRU, a warmup walker, spillback controller, and scheduler integration hooks. Feature flags and runtime knobs are included to tune color count (default 3), warmup sample size, and spill token rate. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed by runtime team (ENG-2498) - [x] unit tests for LRU coloring and warmup walker - [x] integration tests with dedicated scheduler load-simulation harness - [x] perf runs vs baseline on 4 representative workloads - [x] feature flagging + metrics emitted (color-hit-rate, spill-tokens, warmup-success) Performance summary: median tail-latency improvement of 12% on read-heavy mixed-size traces; 95p tail down 18% with a 6% regression in steady-state throughput for extreme continuous write floods (opt-in via knob). Memory fragmentation metric (free-run fragmentation score) improved by ~22% on long-running tenancy tests. Rollback plan: runtime flag disables coloring and warmup and reverts spillback controller; hotfix branch prepared. Related: builds on earlier allocator plumbing (ENG-2001) and complements ongoing work on async compaction.
